title: XML-Based Enterprise Data
learning_outcomes: Describe the purpose of xml-based enterprise data and explain at least one listed subtopic.
Interpret the example related to xml-based enterprise data and predict its expected result.
Identify one validation, compatibility, security, or troubleshooting consideration relevant to the example.

content.intro: In this lesson, you will explore xml-based enterprise data within XML in Real-World Data Formats. You will connect its syllabus topics to an inspectable example, check the expected result, and note tool/version limits.
content.why_it_matters: XML-Based Enterprise Data matters because XML workflows rely on explicit structure and predictable processing. The lesson helps you reason about product catalogs, avoid a common misunderstanding, and make a result reproducible for another developer.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: XML is a family of syntaxes and vocabularies used in practical formats. A file may be one part of a larger package, and its namespace, packaging rules, and host application semantics all matter.

content_blocks.title: Connect the subtopics
content_blocks.text: This lesson explicitly covers: Product catalogs; Orders and invoices; Customer and supplier records; Inter-system data exchange; Schema-driven business validation. Treat these as connected parts of one workflow: define the structure, make the relevant assumptions explicit, and verify a result with a small known input.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: XML-Based Enterprise Data
content_blocks.expected_output: The document has a stable invoice identifier and a line item with quantity and unit-price fields. A schema can make the contract explicit.
content_blocks.run_instructions: Inspect this example as text. Run it only in a processor that supports the shown language/version; the standard CodeLeaf playground previews HTML/CSS/JavaScript only and does not execute XML, XSD, XPath, XSLT, XQuery, Python, or SQL. Inspect the format specification and a minimal valid sample. Do not assume that every XML-based format can be opened as a standalone XML document or edited without preserving package metadata.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Restore the sample to its exact starting state before each experiment. Change one element, attribute, expression, or constraint at a time, then compare the result with the expected behavior.
content_blocks.limitations: This snippet is an inspectable example, not an XML execution service. Validate it with a standards-compatible XML processor; feature support depends on the processor/version.

content_blocks.title: Version and safety checkpoint
content_blocks.text: Distinguish well-formedness, schema validity, and application-level correctness; they are different checks.

content_blocks.title: Try it yourself
content_blocks.text: Create a small synthetic example that demonstrates “Product catalogs”. Then add one boundary case involving “Orders and invoices”. Write down what should happen before testing, and record the exact output or processor message afterward.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming a document is correct because it looks readable.
common_mistakes.why: Visual appearance does not prove well-formedness, schema validity, correct namespace handling, or application-level meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse and validate the document with the intended processor, then assert its meaning using a focused test.

common_mistakes.problem: Mixing specification features with processor support.
common_mistakes.why: A standard may define features that a specific runtime does not implement.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the version and feature support; test with the actual target processor.

common_mistakes.why: Missing values, wrong types, namespace differences, or boundary inputs can expose failures.
common_mistakes.fix: Add a valid case, an invalid case, and an edge case to the verification notes.
